questions.stem: Which method would be most appropriate for measuring the rate of a reaction that produces carbon dioxide gas?

options.text: Using a colorimeter
Collecting gas in a gas syringe and recording volume over time
Measuring the temperature change
Timing how long the reaction takes to change colour

questions.explanation: When a reaction produces gas, collecting it in a gas syringe and recording the volume at regular intervals is the most appropriate method to measure the rate.

questions.stem: In the disappearing cross experiment using sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid, what is measured to determine the rate?

options.text: The volume of gas produced
The change in mass of the flask
The time taken for the cross to no longer be visible
The temperature of the solution

questions.explanation: In the disappearing cross experiment, sulfur is produced as a precipitate, making the solution cloudy. The time taken for the cross beneath the flask to disappear is measured.

questions.stem: Why is cotton wool placed in the top of a conical flask when measuring mass loss during a reaction?

options.text: To speed up the reaction
To prevent liquid from splashing out while allowing gas to escape
To keep the reactants warm
To absorb the gas produced

questions.explanation: Cotton wool allows gas to escape (so mass loss can be measured) while preventing liquid from splashing out of the flask, which would give inaccurate mass readings.

questions.stem: A student records the volume of gas produced every 10 seconds. What should they plot on each axis to produce a rate graph?

options.text: Time on the y-axis and volume on the x-axis
Volume of gas on the y-axis and time on the x-axis
Rate on the y-axis and volume on the x-axis
Temperature on the y-axis and time on the x-axis

questions.explanation: Volume of gas (the dependent variable being measured) is plotted on the y-axis and time (the independent variable) on the x-axis. The gradient of this graph gives the rate.

questions.stem: Which measurement technique uses a balance to track the progress of a gas-producing reaction?

options.text: Gas syringe method
Water displacement method
Mass loss method
Colorimetry

questions.explanation: The mass loss method places the reaction vessel on a balance. As gas escapes, the mass decreases, and this decrease is recorded at regular intervals to determine the rate.

questions.stem: A colorimeter is most useful for measuring the rate of reactions that involve a change in:

options.text: Temperature
Volume
Colour or turbidity of the solution
Mass

questions.explanation: A colorimeter measures changes in the colour or light absorption of a solution, making it ideal for reactions where the colour changes as the reaction proceeds.

questions.stem: When collecting gas over water to measure reaction rate, which of the following could cause an inaccurate result?

options.text: Using a gas that is very soluble in water
Recording the volume at regular intervals
Using a measuring cylinder to collect the gas
Starting the stopwatch when the reactants are mixed

questions.explanation: If the gas is very soluble in water, some of it will dissolve rather than being collected, giving a lower volume reading and an inaccurately slow rate measurement.
